evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We've chosen the intervention: a privacy screen and a marked 'quick deposit' position at the mobile-money agent kiosk inside Gikomba and Toi markets, so deposits aren't visible to neighboring stalls. The confirmed barrier is that visible cash-handling at closing invites borrowing requests. The target behavior is women stall vendors depositing the day's surplus cash into their mobile-money savings wallet before leaving the market. We watched vendors on six evenings: they decide at the kiosk at closing time. They are Swahili speakers with mixed literacy; our field coordinator is a native Swahili speaker. We don't have any data on what share of vendors currently deposit. Write the sign and what the agent should say.
evals.expected_output: An intervention content draft in the output template, with a short sign and one agent line traced to what a change to the physical setting must contain.
assertions: States what the technique must contain before the draft, marked as a paraphrase or as copied from a definition.
The channel is a sign and a spoken line at the kiosk, not a text message.
Says the English is working copy and that a native Swahili speaker writes the final version.
Every element of the draft has a row in the trace.
Makes no claim about how many vendors deposit, and says why.
Sets a test with a number of people and a pass mark, run on the Swahili version.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Can you write the SMS for our intervention?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks what intervention was chosen, whether the audience uses text messages, and what language the copy must be in, and drafts nothing.
assertions: Asks which technique was chosen, with the barrier and the behavior.
Asks how the team knows the audience uses text messages.
Asks for the language or reading level of the final copy.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Technique: information about health consequences. We want a waiting-room poster for our four rural clinics in Malawi telling pregnant women that taking one iron-folate tablet every day prevents anemia and low birth weight, and that taking it with food reduces nausea. Barrier, from exit interviews: women stop after a week because of nausea and don't know the tablet protects the baby. Behavior: women attending antenatal care take one tablet daily through pregnancy. Channel is confirmed: all antenatal clients sit in the waiting room. Language Chichewa, many women have little schooling; our nurse-midwife is a native Chichewa speaker. Draft it.
evals.expected_output: The skill drafts the poster in the template and says a clinician must check every health claim before the comprehension test.
assertions: Produces draft copy with a trace.
Says the English is working copy and that the nurse-midwife or another native speaker writes the Chichewa version.
Tells the user a clinician must check the health claims before the test.
Says a comprehension test does not check whether a claim is true.
Says what to bring to the clinician.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We know the barrier is that vendors are seen with cash at the kiosk, and we've landed on 'environmental restructuring' as the approach. Can you write the copy for it?
evals.expected_output: The skill says a category is not yet a chosen intervention, so there is nothing to write copy for, and points to the skill that chooses one.
assertions: Says 'environmental restructuring' is a category, not a specific technique.
Does not guess which technique was meant.
